fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The psalm says, "Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be moved; it abides forever." (Psalm 125:1) Picture shoving a mountain. You'd pull a muscle before it budged an inch, and I'd be the guy cheering from the sidelines, waving my mustache like a flag.

Careful, friend, this one's flipped. The psalm says the opposite: Mount Zion "…cannot be moved; it abides forever." (Psalm 125:1) A season is about how long a plate of my cookies lasts once the bakery door opens. Forever is a whole other category.

That's it, baker. The psalm says the LORD surrounds His people "…both now and forevermore." (Psalm 125:2) No expiration date stamped on the box. Nothing to check, nothing to toss when the date runs out.

Harder to guess a reason than it looks, friend, and that one isn't in the verse. The reason it gives is "…so that the righteous will not put forth their hands to injustice." (Psalm 125:3) Nothing about the wicked turning in this verse.

That's right. The psalm prays, "Do good, O LORD, to those who are good, and to the upright in heart." (Psalm 125:4) Short and simple. That prayer doesn't need a long wind-up, and I admire that, because I once gave a speech about one cookie and ran out of oven time.
